title: Agentic Knowledge-Model Co-Evolution via Consistency Regularization
title_zh: 基于一致性正则化的智能体知识与模型协同演化

paragraphs.en: LLM agents can evolve by learning from accumulated experience. Existing approaches extract reusable external knowledge, such as skills and memories, from experience to guide subsequent task solving, with some further internalizing this knowledge through model training. However, different ways of analyzing and transforming the same experience can yield knowledge with substantially different utility, even when the resulting guidance appears reasonable. Inspired by consistency regularization, we identify consistent utility gains across different ways of analyzing the same experience, rather than relying on any single way of analyzing it. We introduce SPLICE , a framework for consistency-regularized knowledge-model co-evolution. It constructs evolution views by perturbing how the same experience is analyzed, producing different knowledge candidates. Knowledge updates are then guided by common gain, which accounts for utility gains and their consistency across views. During model evolution, self-distillation internalizes the evolved knowledge alongside reinforcement learning, using knowledge associated with consistent utility degradation as a contrastive reference. The two processes interleave, with model updates driving further knowledge evolution. Experiments across diverse domains show that SPLICE outperforms knowledge evolution and model training baselines by up to 7.1 and 4.6 points in average accuracy, while its evolved knowledge reduces output tokens per correct solution by up to 44% and transfers across model sizes and families.

paragraphs.en: Large Language Model (LLM) agents accumulate experience whenever they reason, use tools, and interact with the environment. For this experience to support continual improvement, an agent must identify useful guidance and reuse it in future tasks. This motivates knowledge evolution, through which agents extract and revise external knowledge, such as skills and memories, from their experience ( Shinn et al., 2023 ; Zhang et al., 2026b ; Ouyang et al., 2026 ; Yang et al., 2026 ) . Such knowledge can also be internalized into model parameters through policy training ( Lu et al., 2026a ; Lu et al., 2026b ; He et al., 2026c ) . The updated model then generates new experience for further knowledge evolution, allowing knowledge and the model to co-evolve ( Xia et al., 2026 ; He et al., 2026b ) . External knowledge thus serves as a medium for agent evolution , connecting accumulated experience with subsequent task solving and model learning.

paragraphs.en: However, knowledge derived from the same experience can differ substantially depending on which evidence is selected and how it is interpreted. For example, analyzing a purchase of the wrong size can yield guidance to include size requirements in queries or verify the selected size before purchase. On a product page that lists the requested size but defaults to another option, the first rule leaves the incorrect selection unchanged, while the second corrects it. Consequently, different ways of analyzing and transforming the same experience can yield knowledge with substantially different utility. Recent studies similarly find that even seemingly reasonable criteria for analyzing and transforming experience can yield less useful knowledge ( Huang et al., 2026 ) , and that plausible knowledge can even underperform using no knowledge at all ( Li et al., 2026a ; Dong et al., 2026 ) . This raises a central question: how can experience be effectively transformed into generalizable knowledge to support agentic evolution?
paragraphs.zh: 然而，从同一经验中得出的知识可能因所选择的证据以及解读方式的不同而存在显著差异。 例如，分析一次买错尺寸的购买行为，可以得出在查询中加入尺寸要求、或在购买前核实所选尺寸的指导。 在一个列出了所需尺寸但默认选中另一选项的商品页面上，第一条规则会保持错误的选择不变，而第二条规则则会纠正它。 因此，对同一经验的不同分析与转化方式所产生的知识，其实用性可能大不相同。 近期研究同样发现，即使是看似合理的经验分析与转化标准，也可能产生实用性较低的知识（Huang et al., 2026），而且看似合理的知识甚至可能不如完全不使用知识（Li et al., 2026a; Dong et al., 2026）。 这引出了一个核心问题：如何才能将经验有效地转化为可泛化的知识，以支持智能体的演化？

paragraphs.en: To tackle this problem, we draw inspiration from consistency regularization (Figure 1 ). This approach encourages consistent predictions for the same input under random parameter perturbations ( Ni et al., 2024 ; Wu et al., 2021 ) . This reduces prediction sensitivity to such perturbations and can improve generalization. Similarly, we view the transformation of experience into knowledge as a function parameterized by textual instructions, whose perturbations define different evolution views. Here, consistency concerns utility: when different views produce distinct knowledge yet yield consistent positive gains on the same tasks, this suggests that the benefits are not specific to a single evolution view. Rather than relying on any single analysis, we therefore use utility consistency across evolution views to guide knowledge evolution toward more generalizable knowledge.

paragraphs.en: We introduce SPLICE , a framework for consistency-regularized knowledge-model co-evolution. During knowledge evolution, it perturbs how the same experience is analyzed and transformed, creating evolution views that each produce a knowledge candidate. Each candidate is evaluated through task replay, and a common gain is calculated by combining utility gain with cross-view consistency. A knowledge optimizer then updates the current knowledge using the candidates and replay trajectories from tasks with the highest common gains. During model evolution, SPLICE combines GRPO ( Shao et al., 2024 ) with self-distillation to internalize the evolved knowledge. The same replay also reveals guidance associated with consistent utility degradation, from which we construct noisy knowledge as a contrastive reference to highlight useful guidance in the evolved knowledge. A token-level gate controls its contribution to retain shared useful guidance. The two processes are interleaved, with the updated model generating new experience for further co-evolution. We evaluate SPLICE on four benchmarks covering math, coding, office work, and web shopping at two model scales. Across these tasks, SPLICE consistently outperforms knowledge evolution and model training baselines, improving average accuracy over the strongest baseline by 3.0 points for Qwen3.5-4B and 4.6 points for Qwen3.5-9B. Notably, its evolved knowledge makes task solving more efficient, requiring up to 44% fewer output tokens per correct solution than the strongest baseline, and delivers larger gains when transferred to other model sizes and families.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出 SPLICE，一个一致性正则化的知识与模型协同演化框架。 在知识演化过程中，SPLICE 对同一段经验的分析与转换方式进行扰动，生成多个演化视角，每个视角产出一份候选知识。 每个候选知识通过任务回放进行评估，并结合效用增益与跨视角一致性计算出一个共同增益。 随后，知识优化器利用这些候选知识以及来自共同增益最高任务的回放轨迹来更新当前知识。 在模型演化过程中，SPLICE 将 GRPO（Shao et al., 2024）与自蒸馏相结合，以内化演化后的知识。 同样的回放还会揭示与一致的效用下降相关联的指导内容，我们据此构造噪声知识作为对比参照，以凸显演化知识中有用的指导。 一个词元级门控控制其贡献，以保留共享的有用指导。 这两个过程交替进行，由更新后的模型生成新经验，以支持进一步的协同演化。 我们在四个覆盖数学、编程、办公事务和网上购物任务的基准上、在两个模型规模上评估 SPLICE。 在这些任务中，SPLICE 持续优于知识演化和模型训练基线，在最强基线的基础上，Qwen3.5-4B 的平均准确率提升 3.0 个百分点，Qwen3.5-9B 提升 4.6 个百分点。 值得注意的是，其演化后的知识使任务求解更加高效，每个正确解所需的输出词元最多比最强基线少 44%，并且在迁移到其他模型规模和模型系列时带来更大的增益。

paragraphs.en: We evaluate SPLICE on four benchmarks from diverse domains: LiveMathBench (LiveMath) ( He et al., 2026a ) for mathematical reasoning, LiveCodeBench (LiveCode) ( Jain et al., 2025 ) for code generation, SpreadsheetBench (SpreadSheet) ( Ma et al., 2024 ) for spreadsheet manipulation, and WebShop ( Yao et al., 2022 ) for interactive web shopping, and report accuracy (Acc.) on the test splits. We compare SPLICE with two groups of baselines. Training-free knowledge evolution methods, including ReasoningBank ( Ouyang et al., 2026 ) , ACE ( Zhang et al., 2026b ) , EvoSkill ( Alzubi et al., 2026 ) , and SkillOpt ( Yang et al., 2026 ) , evolve external knowledge with the task model fixed. Training-based methods include GRPO ( Shao et al., 2024 ) , which optimizes the policy with reinforcement learning, and SkillRL ( Xia et al., 2026 ) and ReSkill ( He et al., 2026b ) , which co-evolve skills with the policy. We also report the base model without knowledge. Details of the benchmarks and baselines are provided in Appendix A .

paragraphs.en: SPLICE spends additional computation on generating multiple evolution views and replaying their candidates. To examine whether its gains come merely from this additional computation, we compare it with two variants that also generate multiple evolution views but use them differently: Best branch adopts the candidate with the highest mean replay reward, and Merge-all updates knowledge with the evidence from all tasks without selection by common gain. As shown in Figure 4 , SPLICE achieves the highest Test Acc. for both model sizes on SpreadSheet and WebShop. Best branch performs worst, suggesting that relying on a single view discards useful evidence, while the evidence merged by Merge-all can be redundant or distracting. The gains of SPLICE thus stem from how common gain uses the evolution views, not from the additional computation alone.
paragraphs.zh: SPLICE 在生成多个演化视图并重放其候选时花费了额外的计算。 为了检验其增益是否仅仅来自这些额外计算，我们将其与两个同样生成多个演化视图但使用方式不同的变体进行比较：Best branch 采用平均重放奖励最高的候选，而 Merge-all 在不按共同增益进行选择的情况下，用来自所有任务的证据更新知识。 如图 4 所示，SPLICE 在 SpreadSheet 和 WebShop 上对于两种模型规模都取得了最高的测试准确率。 Best branch 表现最差，这表明依赖单一视图会丢弃有用的证据，而 Merge-all 合并的证据可能是冗余的或具有干扰性的。 因此，SPLICE 的增益源于共同增益如何使用演化视图，而不仅仅来自额外的计算。

paragraphs.en: Although SPLICE draws on multiple knowledge candidates in each round, we expect its knowledge to be compact but effective, because it retains only updates supported by consistent utility gains across evolution views. To examine whether this holds, we measure the final knowledge length of SPLICE (Know. Evo) and the knowledge evolution baselines, together with the average output tokens and interaction steps over all WebShop test attempts, including failures. As shown in Figure 5 , SPLICE produces knowledge of 4.98k and 6.07k tokens for Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen3.5-9B, respectively, compared with ACE’s 41.51k and 64.99k. Its knowledge is also shorter than EvoSkill’s but longer than SkillOpt’s. SPLICE requires the fewest interaction steps (8.33 and 8.64), suggesting that task-solving efficiency depends on the retained guidance as well as knowledge length. ACE produces shorter outputs with Qwen3.5-4B, but with much longer knowledge and more interaction steps. Table 3 further reports the output tokens per correct attempt, which measures the cost of obtaining a correct solution. SPLICE has the lowest value on both WebShop and LiveCode for both model sizes, reducing it by up to 44% relative to the strongest baseline, indicating that it improves accuracy while reducing the cost of obtaining correct solutions.

paragraphs.en: Just as consistency regularization improves model generalization, we expect utility consistency to yield knowledge that generalizes across task models. To examine whether this holds, we take the final knowledge evolved with Qwen3.5-9B by SPLICE (Know. Evo) and the knowledge evolution baselines, and apply it without further evolution to task models of other sizes (Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen3.5-27B) and other families (Gemma-4-12B-IT ( Gemma Team, 2026 ) and Muse-Glimmer-30B ( Meta Superintelligence Lab, 2026 ) ). We measure absolute Test Acc. gains (in points) over each target model without knowledge on LiveMath and SpreadSheet. As shown in Figure 6 , SPLICE yields the largest mean gain in all settings. On LiveMath, its advantage over the baselines is particularly large for Qwen3.5-4B and Gemma-4-12B-IT: the gains are 31.13 and 33.86 points, respectively, compared with at most 17.38 and 12.42 points for the baselines. Notably, the gains of SPLICE on LiveMath remain at a similar level across all four target models, whereas those of the baselines drop substantially on Qwen3.5-4B and Gemma-4-12B-IT, indicating that the knowledge evolved by SPLICE is less sensitive to which model uses it.

paragraphs.en: Co-evolution trains the model with the evolved knowledge, which raises two questions: whether the model internalizes the knowledge, and how the utility of knowledge changes as the model evolves. Figure 7 evaluates base and trained models on LiveMath with knowledge from different stages. For the first question, the trained models without knowledge already outperform the base models equipped with the final knowledge for both model sizes, reaching 67.88% versus 52.32% with Qwen3.5-9B, indicating that model evolution internalizes and extends the evolved knowledge. For the second question, knowledge brings much smaller gains to the trained models than to the base models, and the early knowledge no longer improves the trained 4B model. The training dynamics in Appendix D show the same trend during training: the benefit of the current knowledge shrinks as the model improves without it. Validating knowledge with the current model before using it for training therefore keeps model evolution from internalizing knowledge that no longer helps.

paragraphs.en: LLM agents improve without parameter updates by turning experience into external knowledge, from textual reflections ( Shinn et al., 2023 ; Zhao et al., 2024 ) to structured memories, playbooks, and skills that are continually updated ( Ouyang et al., 2026 ; Zhang et al., 2026b ; Alzubi et al., 2026 ; Yang et al., 2026 ; Zhang et al., 2026a ) . As such knowledge accumulates, recent studies find that it does not reliably improve task performance ( Li et al., 2026a ; Huang et al., 2026 ; Dong et al., 2026 ) and that seemingly correct experience can mislead future tasks ( Xiong et al., 2026 ) . Some methods therefore retain only updates with positive estimated gain ( Tang et al., 2026 ) , evaluating each candidate on its own. Rather than relying on any single analysis, SPLICE uses utility consistency across evolution views to guide knowledge evolution.
paragraphs.zh: LLM 智能体无需更新参数即可改进，其方式是将经验转化为外部知识，从文本反思（Shinn et al., 2023；Zhao et al., 2024）到持续更新的结构化记忆、操作手册与技能（Ouyang et al., 2026；Zhang et al., 2026b；Alzubi et al., 2026；Yang et al., 2026；Zhang et al., 2026a）。 随着此类知识的积累，近期研究发现它并不能可靠地提升任务表现（Li et al., 2026a；Huang et al., 2026；Dong et al., 2026），而且看似正确的经验可能会误导后续任务（Xiong et al., 2026）。 因此，一些方法只保留估计增益为正的更新（Tang et al., 2026），并对每个候选项单独进行评估。 SPLICE 并不依赖任何单一分析，而是利用跨演化视角的效用一致性来引导知识演化。

paragraphs.en: Knowledge can also be internalized into model parameters through reinforcement learning and self-distillation ( Lu et al., 2026a ; Lu et al., 2026b ; He et al., 2026c ; Lin et al., 2026 ) , or evolved together with the policy ( Xia et al., 2026 ; He et al., 2026b ; Wu et al., 2025 ; Shi et al., 2026 ) . Meanwhile, on-policy self-distillation, in which the model conditioned on privileged context serves as its own teacher ( Zhao et al., 2026a ) , has been refined with token-level modulation ( Li et al., 2026b ) and contrastive references ( Pan et al., 2026 ) . SPLICE constructs its contrastive reference from knowledge that consistently degrades utility during knowledge evolution, and gates it at the token level to retain guidance shared with the evolved knowledge.
paragraphs.zh: 知识还可以通过强化学习和自蒸馏内化到模型参数中（Lu et al., 2026a; Lu et al., 2026b; He et al., 2026c; Lin et al., 2026），或与策略共同演化（Xia et al., 2026; He et al., 2026b; Wu et al., 2025; Shi et al., 2026）。 同时，在策略自蒸馏中，以特权上下文为条件的模型充当自己的教师（Zhao et al., 2026a），该方法已通过词元级调制（Li et al., 2026b）和对比参考（Pan et al., 2026）得到改进。 SPLICE 从知识演化过程中持续降低效用的知识构建其对比参考，并在词元级别对其进行门控，以保留与演化后知识共享的引导。

paragraphs.en: Consistency regularization improves generalization by encouraging consistent predictions for the same input under perturbations. It was first widely adopted in semi-supervised learning ( Bachman et al., 2014 ; Sajjadi et al., 2016 ; Tarvainen and Valpola, 2017 ; Xie et al., 2020 ) and has since been extended to supervised training and fine-tuning of large models ( Wu et al., 2021 ; Ni et al., 2024 ) . paragraphs.en: We introduce SPLICE , a framework for consistency-regularized knowledge-model co-evolution. SPLICE updates knowledge based on utility gains that are consistent across evolution views and internalizes the evolved knowledge through reinforcement learning and gated contrastive self-distillation. Across four benchmarks and two model scales, SPLICE outperforms knowledge evolution and model training baselines, while its evolved knowledge enables more efficient task solving and transfers across model sizes and families. Overall, our results suggest that utility gains consistent across different ways of analyzing experience, rather than those observed under any single analysis, provide an effective signal for turning experience into generalizable knowledge that, when internalized through model evolution, supports long-term agentic evolution.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出 SPLICE，一个一致性正则化的知识与模型协同演化框架。 SPLICE 基于在多个演化视角间保持一致的效用增益来更新知识，并通过强化学习和门控对比自蒸馏将演化后的知识内化到模型中。 在四个基准和两种模型规模上，SPLICE 均优于知识演化和模型训练基线，其演化得到的知识还能实现更高效的任务求解，并在不同规模和不同系列的模型间迁移。 总体而言，我们的结果表明，在不同经验分析方式下保持一致的效用增益，而非任何单一分析下观察到的增益，为将经验转化为可泛化知识提供了有效信号；这些知识通过模型演化被内化后，能够支持智能体的长期演化。

paragraphs.en: Base uses the task model without knowledge. ReasoningBank ( Ouyang et al., 2026 ) stores reasoning memories distilled from experience and retrieves task-relevant entries. ACE ( Zhang et al., 2026b ) maintains an evolving playbook through reflection and curation. EvoSkill ( Alzubi et al., 2026 ) builds skills from task experience, and SkillOpt ( Yang et al., 2026 ) iteratively optimizes external skills. GRPO ( Shao et al., 2024 ) trains the task model with group-relative policy optimization, and SkillRL ( Xia et al., 2026 ) and ReSkill ( He et al., 2026b ) combine skill evolution with policy optimization. All training-based methods are trained for the number of epochs listed in Table 4 .

paragraphs.en: Knowledge evolution and model evolution depend on each other. The utility of knowledge depends on the model that uses it: guidance that helps the current model can become redundant or even harmful after the model is trained. paragraphs.en: (R1) knowledge is evaluated with the model that uses it;

paragraphs.en: A further consideration is efficiency. Knowledge evolution typically requires multiple rounds before it produces stable knowledge with clear utility gains. If model evolution waits for these rounds, training stalls; if it uses knowledge too early, it internalizes weak guidance. The two procedures below handle this trade-off differently. The sequential procedure waits and satisfies both requirements exactly, whereas the asynchronous procedure relaxes R1 during knowledge evolution so that training uses knowledge as soon as it proves useful.
paragraphs.zh: 进一步的考虑是效率问题。 知识演化通常需要多轮才能产生具有明确效用提升的稳定知识。 如果模型演化等待这些轮次完成，训练就会停滞；如果过早使用知识，则会内化较弱的引导。 下面两种流程以不同方式处理这一权衡。 顺序流程选择等待并精确满足两个要求，而异步流程在知识演化期间放宽 R1，使训练在知识被证明有用后即可立即使用。

sents.en: The sequential procedure waits and satisfies both requirements exactly, whereas the asynchronous procedure relaxes R1 during knowledge evolution so that training uses knowledge as soon as it proves useful.

paragraphs.en: The sequential procedure (Algorithm 1 ) alternates the two processes. Knowledge evolution runs with the model fixed, so every candidate is replayed and validated with the model that will use it. It continues until M M consecutive updates are rejected, indicating that knowledge evolution no longer improves the knowledge under the current model. Model evolution then performs T T updates with K K and K − K^{-} fixed. The rejected rounds share the same model and knowledge, and thus provide a common baseline for constructing K − K^{-} from consistent utility degradation (§ 3.2 ). Afterwards, knowledge evolution continues from the current K K with experience collected by the updated model.
paragraphs.zh: 序贯流程（算法 1）交替进行这两个过程。 知识演化在模型固定的情况下运行，因此每个候选知识都用将要使用它的模型来重放和验证。 该过程持续进行，直到连续 M M 次更新被拒绝，表明在当前模型下知识演化不再能改进知识。 随后，模型演化在 K K 和 K − K^{-} 固定的情况下执行 T T 次更新。 被拒绝的各轮次共享相同的模型和知识，因此为基于一致效用下降来构建 K − K^{-} 提供了共同基线（§ 3.2）。 之后，知识演化从当前 K K 出发，利用更新后的模型收集的经验继续进行。

paragraphs.en: The asynchronous procedure (Algorithm 2 ) runs knowledge evolution and model evolution at the same time. paragraphs.en: Two design choices limit this effect. Knowledge evolution uses recent experience, which keeps the model change between experience collection and replay small. More importantly, knowledge enters training only after it improves validation performance over no knowledge with the current model, so an update whose apparent gain comes from the model update is not adopted unless it also helps the current model. The remaining cost is efficiency: a shifted threshold can select less informative tasks and produce updates that are later rejected. Compared with the sequential procedure, the asynchronous procedure accepts this cost in exchange for using knowledge without waiting for knowledge evolution to finish.

paragraphs.en: LLM agents can improve without parameter updates by turning experience into external knowledge. Early methods reflect on failures and store textual lessons: Reflexion keeps verbal self-reflections for subsequent attempts ( Shinn et al., 2023 ) , ExpeL extracts insights from successful and failed trajectories across tasks ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) , CLIN maintains a textual memory updated across trials ( Majumder et al., 2023 ) , and Agent-Pro reflects at the level of the agent’s policy ( Zhang et al., 2024 ) . Another line accumulates procedural knowledge, such as executable skill libraries ( Wang et al., 2023 ) , workflows induced from past trajectories ( Wang et al., 2024 ) , and skills that are automatically discovered and refined ( Alzubi et al., 2026 ; Yang et al., 2026 ; Wei et al., 2026 ) , including learnable memory operations ( Zhang et al., 2026a ) . Other methods maintain structured memories or contexts that evolve during task solving, including agentic memory organization ( Xu et al., 2026 ) , adaptive test-time memory ( Suzgun et al., 2026 ) , reasoning strategies distilled from successes and failures ( Ouyang et al., 2026 ) , and evolving playbooks ( Zhang et al., 2026b ) . Training-Free GRPO further distills experiential knowledge from group-relative comparisons of rollouts ( Cai et al., 2025 ) . Related studies examine the reliability of skills and agentic reasoning: model-generated skills do not reliably improve performance ( Li et al., 2026a ; Huang et al., 2026 ; Dong et al., 2026 ) , unchecked accumulation degrades skill retrieval ( Zhang et al., 2026c ) , and agents can fail to use experience and external evidence reliably ( Xiong et al., 2026 ; Zhao et al., 2026b ) . Some methods therefore retain only updates with positive estimated gain ( Tang et al., 2026 ) . SPLICE focuses on which evidence should drive a knowledge update, using utility consistency across multiple evolution views of the same experience.

paragraphs.en: Internalizing knowledge into model parameters is closely related to context distillation, which trains a model without a context to match its predictions with the context ( Snell et al., 2022 ) , and to on-policy distillation, which supervises a student on its own generated trajectories ( Agarwal et al., 2024 ) . For LLM agents, recent work internalizes skills into the policy through reinforcement learning and self-distillation ( Lu et al., 2026a ; He et al., 2026c ) , progressively reduces reliance on skills provided in context ( Lu et al., 2026b ) , or attributes success to skills by contrasting rollouts with and without them ( Lin et al., 2026 ) . Other work evolves knowledge together with the policy: skill banks are updated during online reinforcement learning ( Xia et al., 2026 ) , skill creation is coupled with policy optimization ( He et al., 2026b ) , experience is distilled into principles that guide further policy learning ( Wu et al., 2025 ) , and a single policy learns to select, use, and distill skills ( Shi et al., 2026 ) . On-policy self-distillation, in which the model conditioned on privileged context serves as its own teacher, has become a dense training signal for LLMs ( Zhao et al., 2026a ) . Since privileged context can distort the teacher’s token distribution, recent variants modulate token-level guidance by teacher–student disagreement ( Li et al., 2026b ) , reverse the distillation direction ( Shen et al., 2026 ) , or contrast signals under correct and wrong hints ( Pan et al., 2026 ) . Negative signals have likewise been shown to provide useful supervision in reinforcement learning for LLMs ( Zhu et al., 2026 ) . SPLICE derives its negative reference from knowledge evolution itself, using knowledge associated with consistent utility degradation, and combines it with task-level weighting and a token-level gate during internalization.
paragraphs.zh: 将知识内化到模型参数中与上下文蒸馏密切相关，后者训练模型在没有上下文的情况下使其预测与有上下文时的预测保持一致（Snell et al., 2022），也与在线策略蒸馏相关，后者在智能体自身生成的轨迹上对学生模型进行监督（Agarwal et al., 2024）。 对于大语言模型智能体，近期的工作通过强化学习和自蒸馏将技能内化到策略中（Lu et al., 2026a；He et al., 2026c），逐步减少对上下文中提供的技能的依赖（Lu et al., 2026b），或者通过对比有技能和无技能的 rollout 来将成功归因于技能（Lin et al., 2026）。 另一些工作则让知识与策略共同演化：在在线强化学习期间更新技能库（Xia et al., 2026），将技能创建与策略优化相耦合（He et al., 2026b），将经验蒸馏为指导后续策略学习的原则（Wu et al., 2025），或者让单一策略学会选择、使用和蒸馏技能（Shi et al., 2026）。 在线策略自蒸馏中，以特权上下文为条件的模型充当自己的教师，这已成为大语言模型的一种密集训练信号（Zhao et al., 2026a）。 由于特权上下文可能扭曲教师模型的词元分布，近期的变体通过师生分歧来调节词元级指导（Li et al., 2026b），逆转蒸馏方向（Shen et al., 2026），或对正确提示与错误提示下的信号进行对比（Pan et al., 2026）。 负信号同样已被证明可以在大语言模型的强化学习中提供有用的监督（Zhu et al., 2026）。 SPLICE 的负参考源自知识演化本身，利用与效用持续下降相关联的知识，并在内化过程中将其与任务级加权和词元级门控相结合。

paragraphs.en: Consistency regularization encourages a model to make consistent predictions for the same input under perturbations. In semi-supervised learning, early methods enforce agreement under stochastic transformations, dropout, and ensembling ( Bachman et al., 2014 ; Sajjadi et al., 2016 ; Laine and Aila, 2016 ) , and later methods improve the targets with weight-averaged teachers ( Tarvainen and Valpola, 2017 ) or strong data augmentation ( Xie et al., 2020 ) . The idea has been extended to supervised training and fine-tuning through consistency between dropout sub-models ( Wu et al., 2021 ) or under parameter perturbations ( Ni et al., 2024 ) . These methods assume that the correct output is invariant to the perturbation and enforce consistency through a training loss. In knowledge evolution, this assumption does not hold at the level of content, since different evolution views are expected to produce different knowledge. SPLICE therefore requires consistency only in the utility gains of the resulting knowledge and uses it as a criterion for selecting evidence.
paragraphs.zh: 一致性正则化鼓励模型对同一输入在扰动下做出一致的预测。 在半监督学习中，早期方法在随机变换、dropout 和集成下强制一致性（Bachman et al., 2014；Sajjadi et al., 2016；Laine and Aila, 2016），后来的方法通过权重平均的教师（Tarvainen and Valpola, 2017）或强数据增强（Xie et al., 2020）来改进目标。 这一思想已被扩展到监督训练和微调中，通过 dropout 子模型之间的一致性（Wu et al., 2021）或参数扰动下的一致性（Ni et al., 2024）来实现。 这些方法假设正确输出对扰动是不变的，并通过训练损失来强制一致性。 在知识演化中，这一假设在内容层面并不成立，因为不同的演化视角预期会产生不同的知识。 因此 SPLICE 只要求所得知识在效用增益上保持一致，并将其作为选择证据的准则。

In contrast, the updates proposed by SPLICE mostly stay close to zero or positive and have the smallest mean absolute change for both model sizes. This is consistent with the design of common gain, which discounts evidence whose gains appear under only some evolution views and thus avoids updates that change the knowledge in unstable ways.

paragraphs.en: To examine how proposed updates affect individual tasks, we compare each proposed update with the current knowledge on the validation tasks. Error correction is the percentage of tasks failed under the current knowledge that the proposed update solves, and success preservation is the percentage of tasks solved under the current knowledge that remain solved. Figure 9 reports both metrics for the proposed updates in the first 30 evolution rounds on WebShop, excluding rounds without an update. SPLICE attains the highest pooled rates for both metrics: 23.60% error correction and 75.94% success preservation with Qwen3.5-4B, and 17.75% and 77.47% with Qwen3.5-9B, whereas the best baseline preservation rates are 68.40% and 64.79%. Updates selected by common gain thus correct more errors while breaking fewer existing successes.

paragraphs.en: Figure 10 (left) tracks validation Acc. on LiveMath during co-evolution, evaluating the model without knowledge and with the latest knowledge at each optimizer update step. Early in training, the knowledge improves the model substantially. As the model improves without knowledge, this benefit shrinks, and some knowledge updates no longer improve the current model and are rejected. The examples on the right illustrate both directions of this interplay. For the 4B model, the same knowledge helps the model answer correctly at update step 44, but by update step 56 the model answers correctly without it, whereas adding the knowledge leads to an error. For the 9B model, a check learned from execution feedback corrects an unsupported convergence claim on another task: at update step 32, the model answers incorrectly without knowledge and correctly with it, and the knowledge is accepted for subsequent training. These dynamics motivate validating knowledge with the current model before using it for training (Appendix B ).
